method: Builds a .mount unit from a mount point, a What= source, an optional file system type and a comma-separated option list, and can add the matching .automount unit for on-demand mounting. The unit file name is escaped from the mount point exactly as systemd escapes it: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, ':', '_' and '.' are kept (a leading dot is written \x2e), every slash becomes '-', and every other character becomes one \xHH escape per UTF-8 byte, so /mnt/My Backup becomes mnt-My\x20Backup.mount. Duplicate and trailing slashes and '.' components are normalized away, '..' is refused instead of simplified, the root path is refused because the root filesystem is mounted before systemd starts, and a name longer than the 255 characters systemd allows is refused. What= accepts an absolute device or image path, UUID=/LABEL=/PARTUUID=/PARTLABEL=/ID= identifiers, a host:/export specification for network file systems, or tmpfs, and refuses spaces, backslashes and percent signs. Options= tokens accept letters, digits and _ . : = + @ / - only; empty tokens, embedded spaces, duplicates and x-systemd. options are refused, the last because systemd-fstab-generator reads those only from /etc/fstab and silently ignores them in a unit file. Type= may be left empty to rely on detection. The builder emits [Unit], [Mount] and - unless an automount unit is requested - [Install] WantedBy= on the chosen target; the automount unit carries [Automount] Where=, an optional TimeoutIdleSec= and the [Install] section, while the .mount it activates deliberately has none, and the install command enables whichever unit was generated. Warnings name the automatic ordering of network mounts (after network-online.target, before remote-fs.target), of tmpfs mounts (after swap.target) and the effect of nofail, which stops the mount from being ordered before local-fs.target. The tool does not verify that the source device exists, that the mount point is empty, or that the file system type is right, and it never runs mount, umount or systemctl.
